newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares fall on U.S. rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares fall on U.S. rate worries.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Thursday amid concerns after U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan opened for possible rate hikes at the Federal Open Market Committe (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday.
The exchange's general index fell 1.66 percent to 2,627.69 in turnover of 5.14 billion crowns.
"If the market falls further in the U.S. tonight, it could be a proper circus tomorrow," a trader said. "I have difficulty seeing that there would be any upside tomorrow."
The downturn pulled many blue chips along, such as drugs major Astra and telecoms group Ericsson.
Ericsson dropped seven crowns to 247.5 crowns and Astra fell seven to 345.

Banking group Nordbanken dipped ten crowns to 257 crowns, while rival S-E-Banken managed to close unchanged at 83 crowns. Nordbanken's chief executive said on Thursday that he was prepared to take up merger talks with S-E-Banken again if owners agreed.
Appliance maker Electrolux fell 10.5 crowns to 460 crowns and forestry group MoDo plunged 17.5 crowns to 219.5 crowns.
